answer: One way is to make each identity expensive to fake. Before an agent can trade or vote, it has to lock a small refundable stake and build a record of real work over time, like timber seasoning slowly instead of arriving ready-made. A sybil farm would have to pay that cost for every fake, and its history would look thin and hollow, like karst riddled with gaps, while a genuine agent's record stays solid, like marble. The stake plus the time cost makes flooding the network unprofitable.
